newsitem.title: INDIA: Foreign funds drive Bombay shr index up 3.35 pct.
newsitem.headline: Foreign funds drive Bombay shr index up 3.35 pct.

text.p: Share prices soared for the second successive day at the Bombay bourses on Wednesday as foreign institutional investors (FIIs) also turned buyers, brokers said.
The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) top 30 share index leapt 108.23 points, or 3.35 percent, to 3,335.36 provisional close.
The rally followed a 96.92 points rise on Tuesday sparked by a freer credit policy announced by the central bank at the long weekend which set off cuts in lending rates by banks.
The 50-share National Stock Exchange (NSE) index rose 34.35 points or 3.74 percent to 953.35 and the CRISIL-500 index rose 18.96 points or 3.07 percent to 636.24, both provisional close.
Fewer sellers and buying by FIIs and local punters triggered the sharp rise, traders said.
"There was supply mismatch," said a trader. "There were more buyers at (BSE index of) 3,300 than when it was 3,000."

Top stocks TISCO rallied 17.50 rupees to 192.75, SBI 11.25 to 240, Bajaj Auto 25.0 to 996.50, ACC 95.75 to 1,645.75, ITC 11.75 to 322.50, TELCO 12.50 to 442.25, Indian Hotel 22.25 to 653.50, Hind Lever 10.50 to 825 and Reliance 8.0 to 214.75.
Other blue-chip stocks like Oriental Bank, Carrier Aircon, Nestle, MTNL, VSNL, Wartsila, BPCL, Glaxo, Cipla, CESC were some that attracted good demand, traders said.
Analysts expect the volatile market to cool towards week's end when profit-takers get active.
"I don't see the rally ... sustaining for very long," Vikas Saraf, research head at SSKI Securities, told Reuters.
"None of the major indications on the economic front have changed. We still see a lot of question marks around," said Sanjay Agarwal, chief executive of Lloyds Securities.
"The outlook is cautious. The 3,350 mark is a level where we have to wait and watch to see if the rally sustains," he said.
